chunks: And with this chain, from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Paradise is made obligatory for one who feeds a hungry person.

key_terms.أَشْبَعَ: to satisfy the hunger of / to feed fully
key_terms.كَبِدًا: liver (metonymy for the self/soul, indicating deep hunger)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for feeding a hungry person according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Thawab al-Amal, Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), highlighting the juridical weight of feeding the hungry by using the term 'wajib' (obligated), which implies a guaranteed entry into Paradise rather than merely a recommended reward. This act is viewed in Shia tradition as a direct fulfillment of the rights of the poor (Huquq al-Nas), serving as a tangible manifestation of gratitude for divine sustenance and a means of purifying one's wealth and soul.
